title: Tokyo to Osaka EV Road Trip: Japan's Golden Route by Electric Car — Complete Family Itinerary
excerpt: Japan's iconic Tokyo-Osaka corridor is now fully EV-ready. This 6-day family itinerary covers Nagoya's museums, Kyoto's temples, and Nara's deer park — with detailed charging stops at every leg. Costs, rental tips, and highway station guides included.
author: EV Charging Asia Team
content:
# Tokyo to Osaka EV Road Trip: Japan's Golden Route by Electric Car

The Tokyo to Osaka corridor — Japan's Golden Route — is the country's most famous road trip. It links two of the world's largest cities via the Tomei and Meishin expressways, passing Mt. Fuji, Shizuoka's tea fields, Nagoya's castle, and Kyoto's thousand-year-old temples.

And the best news for EV drivers? Japan's highway charging network has reached critical mass. With CHAdeMO and CCS fast chargers at nearly every major service area, you can drive the entire 500 km route with zero range anxiety — and save a fortune compared to the Shinkansen for a family of four.

## Route Overview

| Detail | Info |
|--------|------|
| Distance | ~510 km (Tokyo → Osaka via Tomei Expressway) |
| Driving time (direct) | 6-7 hours without breaks |
| Recommended duration | 5-6 days (family itinerary) |
| Charging stops needed | 2-3 per direction |
| Best EV for trip | Any EV with 350+ km WLTP range |
| Toll cost (one way) | ~¥12,000 ($80 USD) |
| Charging cost (one way) | ~¥3,000-4,500 ($20-30 USD) |
| Best time to go | March-May (cherry blossom) or October-November (autumn colours) |

## Why Drive Instead of the Shinkansen?

| Factor | EV Road Trip | Shinkansen (Nozomi) |
|--------|-------------|---------------------|
| Cost for family of 4 (one way) | ¥15,000-17,000 | ¥58,000-72,000 |
| Door-to-door time | 6 days (includes sightseeing) | ~3 hours (station-to-station only) |
| Flexibility | Stop anywhere, carry unlimited luggage | Fixed schedule, luggage limited |
| Experience | Scenic, family bonding, adventure | Efficient but impersonal |

## Before You Go: Renting an EV in Japan

### Best EV Rental Options

| Company | EVs Available | Features | Price/Day |
|---------|--------------|----------|-----------|
| **Times Car Rental** | Nissan Sakura, Nissan Leaf, Tesla Model 3 | Largest network, English support, highway passes included | ¥8,000-15,000 |
| **Nippon Rent-A-Car** | Nissan Leaf e+, Nissan Sakura | Airport locations, ETC card included | ¥7,000-12,000 |
| **Tesla Rentals Tokyo** | Tesla Model 3/Y | English support, includes CCS2 adapter | ¥15,000-25,000 |
| **EV Rentals Japan** | Nissan Leaf e+, Tesla Model 3 | Specialised EV rental, English guides available | ¥10,000-18,000 |

**Recommendation for families:** The **Nissan Leaf e+** (62 kWh, 458 km WLTP) is ideal. It has CHAdeMO (Japan's standard fast-charge connector), plenty of space for luggage, and ISOFIX mounts for child seats. The **Nissan Sakura** (20 kWh, 180 km) is too short-range for this trip unless you want to charge every 90 minutes.

### Essential Pre-Trip Checklist

- [ ] **ETC Card** — required for expressway entry. Most rental companies include one. It works at automated toll gates.
- [ ] **International Driving Permit (IDP)** — mandatory for non-Japanese licenses. Get it before leaving your home country.
- [ ] **Download Enel X Way Japan app** — the primary app for CHAdeMO charging. Works with international credit cards.
- [ ] **Download e-Mobility Power app** — backup network, covers Nissan dealership chargers.
- [ ] **Download PlugShare** — community reports on charger status.
- [ ] **Purchase an e-Mobility Power card** — available at FamilyMart convenience stores. Speeds up charging at some stations.
- [ ] **Pack a Type 2 AC cable** — for overnight charging at hotels.

### How Charging Works on Japanese Expressways

Japanese highway service areas (SA) and parking areas (PA) have dedicated EV charging bays. Located near toilets or convenience stores.

- **CHAdeMO 50kW** — the standard. 20-80% in ~45 min for a Leaf e+.
- **CCS 90kW** — newer stations. 20-80% in ~25 min.
- **Cost:** ¥30-50 per minute (CHAdeMO), or ¥350-700 per session (flat rate for 30 min at CCS).
- **Usage:** Park, plug in, tap your Enel X Way card or scan QR in the app. You must move your car when charging is complete — some stations charge ¥200/minute idle fee.

## The Route: Day-by-Day Family Itinerary

### Day 1: Tokyo — Pick Up EV, Explore, and Prepare

**Morning:** Pick up your rental EV in Tokyo (Shinagawa or Tokyo Station area). Charge to 100% at **Tokyo Station Yaesu Parking** (CHAdeMO 50kW — 4 slots) or at your hotel if they have charging.

**Family activities in Tokyo:**
- **teamLab Borderless (Azabudai Hills)** — immersive digital art museum. Kids are mesmerised by the interactive light installations. Allow 2-3 hours. Book tickets online to skip queues.
- **Ueno Zoo** — Japan's oldest zoo. Giant pandas, polar bears, and a monorail that kids love. ¥600 adults, free for children under 12.
- **Odaiba** — man-made island with Toyota Mega Web (car museums, test tracks), Legoland Discovery Center, and the giant Gundam statue at DiverCity.

**Charging:** Overnight at hotel — confirm AC 7-22kW availability. Many Tokyo hotels now offer EV charging for guests.

**Overnight:** Tokyo — Shinagawa or Tokyo Station area.

### Day 2: Tokyo → Shizuoka/Mt. Fuji Area (160 km, 2-3 hours)

**Morning (8 AM):** Leave Tokyo early to beat traffic. Take the **Tomei Expressway** west. The Tokyo-Yokohama stretch can be congested 7-9 AM — leave by 7:30 AM at the latest.

**Charging Stop 1: Ebina Service Area (37 km, 30 min from Tokyo)**
- **Chargers:** CHAdeMO 50kW + CCS 90kW — 6 slots
- **Charge time:** 20-30 min (depending on starting charge)
- **Why stop:** Ebina SA is the best family stop on the Tomei. Huge food court with kids' meals, clean restrooms with baby-changing stations, convenience store, and a dog run that kids enjoy watching. Grab breakfast: the Ebina **Mega Melon Pan** (giant melon bread) is a must-try.
- **Pro tip:** If you left with 90%+, skip Ebina and stop at the next SA instead.

**Scenic option — Lake Ashi / Hakone (detour):** If you want to see Mt. Fuji up close, take the Hakone Turnpike exit at Gotemba (Km 100). The **Hakone Skyline** viewpoint has stunning Mt. Fuji views on clear days. Allow 2 hours for the detour.

**Charging Stop 2: Fuji River Service Area (140 km, 1.5 hours from Tokyo)**
- **Chargers:** CHAdeMO 50kW — 4 slots
- **Charge time:** 15 min (top-up)
- **Why stop:** Views of the Fuji River valley. Small but clean rest area with a convenience store. The observation deck has iconic Mt. Fuji views if the weather is clear.

**Arrive Shizuoka City or Fujinomiya (afternoon, ~160 km)**

Shizuoka is the heart of Japan's tea country. The area between Shizuoka City and Fujinomiya offers the closest accessible views of Mt. Fuji.

**Family activities in Shizuoka area:**
- **Nihondaira Yume Terrace** — panoramic platform with Mt. Fuji and Suruga Bay views. The glass-walled observation area is stunning. Free entry.
- **Nihondaira Ropeway** — cable car connecting Nihondaira to the Kunozan Toshogu Shrine. The shrine itself is a gorgeous gold-leaf building. Family ticket (2 adults + 2 kids): ¥2,500.
- **Fujinomiya City** — the closest city to Mt. Fuji's southern trailhead. Visit **Shiraito Falls** (a 30-minute drive) — a stunning 150-metre-wide waterfall. Free entry.
- **Green Tea Tour** — many tea farms offer free or ¥500 tours. The kids can try matcha ice cream while you learn about Shizuoka's famous green tea.

**Charging in Shizuoka:**
| Station | Location | Speed | Slots | Notes |
|---------|----------|-------|-------|-------|
| Nihondaira Hotel (overnight guest) | Nihondaira | AC 6kW | 2 | Confirm at booking |
| Shizuoka Station (North) | City centre | CHAdeMO 50kW | 2 | Near restaurants |
| Fujinomiya City Hall | Fujinomiya | CHAdeMO 50kW | 2 | Free parking for 2 hours |

**Overnight:** **Nihondaira Hotel** (family rooms, EV charging, hot springs with Mt. Fuji views on clear days) or a ryokan in the area.

**Dinner:** Try **Shizuoka oden** — a local take on Japanese stew with seafood, eggs, and vegetables in a dark soy broth. Very kid-friendly. The **Aoisa Cafe** near Nihondaira has excellent local cuisine.

### Day 3: Shizuoka → Nagoya (190 km, 2.5 hours)

**Morning (8:30 AM):** Optional: sunrise at **Miho no Matsubara** (a UNESCO-protected pine grove beach with Mt. Fuji views). One of Japan's most photographed scenes. Then hit the Tomei eastward toward Nagoya.

**Charging Stop: Hamamatsu Service Area (75 km from Shizuoka, 1 hour)**
- **Chargers:** CHAdeMO 50kW + CCS 90kW — 6 slots
- **Charge time:** 20-30 min
- **Why stop:** Hamamatsu is where the Tomei meets the coast. Large SA with a food court, souvenir shop, and small children's play area. The **Hamamatsu gyoza** from the food court is famous — worth trying.

**Optional detour: Hamamatsu City (10 min off highway)**
- **Hamamatsu Flower Park** — huge flower garden with a 130m-long "flower curtain" in spring.
- **Hamamatsu Museum of Musical Instruments** — one of the world's best. Kids can try playing instruments.

**Continue to Nagoya (120 km from Hamamatsu, 1.5 hours)**

**Arrive Nagoya (~1:00 PM):** Japan's fourth-largest city, home to Toyota, incredible food, and world-class museums for kids.

**Family activities in Nagoya:**
- **Nagoya Castle** — reconstructed castle with stunning golden shachihoko (tiger-fish) roof ornaments. The castle museum has hands-on exhibits where kids can try on samurai armour and lift 30-kg swords. ¥500 adults, kids free.
- **SCMAGLEV and Railway Park** — a train museum operated by JR Central. Massive scale models, train simulators, and the actual Maglev test vehicle. This is HEAVEN for train-obsessed kids. ¥1,000 adults, ¥500 children.
- **Toyota Commemorative Museum of Industry and Technology** — interactive exhibits on weaving and car manufacturing. Kids get a "factory passport" and stamp stations throughout the museum. Free for children under 15.
- **Port of Nagoya Public Aquarium** — one of Japan's largest. The main tank has whale sharks and manta rays. Dolphin and orca shows throughout the day. ¥2,000 adults, ¥1,000 children.
- **Nagoya City Science Museum** — the world's largest planetarium dome (35m!). Interactive science experiments on every floor.

**Charging in Nagoya:**
| Station | Location | Speed | Slots | Notes |
|---------|----------|-------|-------|-------|
| Nagoya Station (Tsubomi Parking) | Station area | CHAdeMO 50kW + CCS 50kW | 4 | Central, large parking, near mall |
| AEON Mall Nagoya | 15 min from centre | CHAdeMO 50kW | 6 | Charge while shopping/dining |
| Nagoya Marriott Associa Hotel | Connected to station | AC 6kW | 2 | Midori no Sato card needed |
| Midland Square | City centre | CHAdeMO 50kW | 2 | Near restaurants |

**Recommended overnight:** **Nagoya Marriott Associa Hotel** (connected to Nagoya Station — easiest EV access). Or a family-friendly hotel with AC charging.

**Dinner:** Nagoya is famous for its unique food culture. Try:
- **Hitsumabushi** — grilled eel on rice, served three ways (plain, with condiments, with tea). Very kid-friendly.
- **Nagoya Cochin** — local chicken, used in yakitori and karaage.
- **Kishimen** — flat udon noodles in soy broth. Perfect for kids.

### Day 4: Nagoya → Kyoto (140 km, 2 hours)

**Morning:** Explore Nagoya's castle or railway park, then depart south.

**Charging Stop: Suzuka Circuit Service Area (75 km, 1 hour from Nagoya)**
- **Chargers:** CHAdeMO 50kW + CCS 90kW — 4 slots
- **Charge time:** 20 min (top-up recommended)
- **Why stop:** Suzuka SA is on the Meishin Expressway. It offers views of the Suzuka Circuit (F1 track). Small play area for kids. This is the last reliable charger before Kyoto.

**Arrive Kyoto (~1:00 PM):** Japan's cultural heart. Park your EV and use public transport for the day — Kyoto's temples are best explored on foot or by bus.

**Family activities in Kyoto (walkable from central Kyoto):**
- **Fushimi Inari Shrine** — thousands of vermilion torii gates snaking up a mountainside. The entrance area is crowded but the gates thin out after 20 minutes uphill. Allow 2 hours. Free entry. Kids love running through the gates.
- **Kinkaku-ji (Golden Pavilion)** — the iconic gold-leaf temple reflected in a pond. ¥500 adults, free for children. 30-60 minutes.
- **Arashiyama Bamboo Grove** — walk through towering bamboo. Nearby **Arashiyama Monkey Park** is a steep 20-minute climb but the monkeys are free-roaming and the view over Kyoto is spectacular. ¥550 adults, ¥250 children.
- **Nintendo Museum (near Kyoto Station)** — opening hours vary, book weeks in advance. Interactive exhibits on Nintendo's history from Hanafuda cards to Switch.
- **Kyoto Railway Museum** — massive train museum with actual steam, diesel, and Shinkansen trains you can board and explore. Kids can operate a train simulator. ¥1,500 adults, ¥300 children.

**Charging in Kyoto:**
| Station | Location | Speed | Slots | Notes |
|---------|----------|-------|-------|-------|
| Kyoto Station AVANTI Parking | Station area | CHAdeMO 50kW + CCS 50kW | 4 | Best — central, large lot |
| Aeon Mall Kyoto | 15 min bus from centre | CHAdeMO 50kW | 6 | Option for overnight shoppers |
| Kiyomizudera Temple parking | Temple entrance | CHAdeMO 50kW | 2 | Limited — arrive early |

**Overnight:** **Hotel Granvia Kyoto** (connected to Kyoto Station — EV parking available, reserve ahead) or a machiya (traditional townhouse) rental.

**Evening:** **Pontocho Alley** — narrow lantern-lit alley along the Kamo River. Grab yakitori from a street stall or book a traditional kaiseki dinner.

### Day 5: Kyoto → Nara → Osaka (100 km total, 2 hours driving)

**Morning (8:30 AM):** Drive south to Nara (45 km, 45 min from Kyoto). Take the Meihan National Highway.

**Arrive Nara (9:30 AM):**

**Nara Park** — the highlight. Over 1,200 tame sika deer roam freely. Buy shika-senbei (deer crackers, ¥200) from stalls and feed them. The deer bow when you feed them — kids go wild for this.

- **Todai-ji Temple** — houses a 15-metre-tall bronze Buddha statue. The building is the world's largest wooden structure. ¥600 adults, ¥300 children.
- **Kasuga Taisha Shrine** — thousands of stone and bronze lanterns lining the path. Atmospheric and beautiful.
- **Nara National Museum** — Buddhist art. Free for kids under 18.

**Lunch:** Nara is famous for **kakinoha-zushi** (sushi wrapped in persimmon leaves) and **Nara chazuke** (green tea over rice). Both are mild and kid-friendly.

**Charging in Nara:**
- **Nara Park Parking Lot** — CHAdeMO 50kW, 2 slots. Near the park entrance.
- **AEON Mall Nara** — 10 min drive, CHAdeMO 50kW, 4 slots.

**Afternoon: Nara → Osaka (40 km, 45 min)**

Take the Nishi-Meihan Expressway. Short and easy drive.

**Arrive Osaka (3:00 PM):** Japan's food capital.

**Family activities in Osaka:**
- **Universal Studios Japan** — world-class theme park with Super Nintendo World. Express passes recommended during peak season. Book on Klook for discounts. The park has EV charging in its main parking lot (CHAdeMO 50kW, 6 slots).
- **Osaka Aquarium Kaiyukan** — one of the world's largest aquariums. Giant whale sharks, a 9-metre deep Pacific tank, and touch pools. ¥2,700 adults, ¥1,400 children. 2-3 hours.
- **Dotonbori** — the iconic neon-lit canal district. Take a family photo under the Glico Running Man sign. Street food: takoyaki (octopus balls), okonomiyaki (savoury pancakes), and kushikatsu (deep-fried skewers). Kids eat well in Osaka.
- **Osaka Castle** — impressive castle with a museum inside. The observation deck on the 8th floor has great views. ¥600 adults, free for children.
- **Kids Plaza Osaka** — a hands-on museum designed entirely for children. Three floors of interactive exhibits: a fantasy castle, a mini city, and a science lab. ¥1,400 adults, ¥600 children. Plan 3-4 hours.
- **Tsutenkaku Tower** — retro observation tower in Shinsekai. The distinctive design and surrounding retro neighbourhood are a hit with kids. ¥900 adults, ¥400 children.

**Charging in Osaka:**
| Station | Location | Speed | Slots | Notes |
|---------|----------|-------|-------|-------|
| Universal Studios Japan Parking | USJ entrance | CHAdeMO 50kW + CCS 50kW | 6 | Charge while you ride! |
| Osaka Station (Osaka Sta. City) | Umeda | CHAdeMO 50kW + CCS 50kW | 6 | Best central option |
| AEON Mall Osaka Dome | 10 min from centre | CHAdeMO 50kW | 4 | Large parking lot |
| Namba Parks | Namba | CHAdeMO 50kW | 2 | Near Dotonbori |

**Recommended overnight with EV charging:**
| Hotel | Charging | Family Features | Price/Night |
|-------|----------|----------------|-------------|
| **Hotel Nikko Osaka** | AC 6kW (reserve ahead) | Central near Shinsaibashi, family rooms | ¥15,000-25,000 |
| **Ritz-Carlton Osaka** | CHAdeMO 50kW (2 slots) | Kids amenities, pool, central | ¥30,000-50,000 |
| **Holiday Inn Namba** | AC 6kW (1 slot) | Namba location, family-friendly | ¥10,000-15,000 |
| **Universal Port** | AC 6kW | Steps from USJ, colourful rooms | ¥15,000-30,000 |

### Day 6: Return Journey or Fly Out

**Option A: Return Drive to Tokyo (510 km, 6-7 hours driving)**
- Leave Osaka by 7:00 AM.
- Charge at **Suzuka Circuit SA** (75 km) — 20 min.
- Charge at **Hamamatsu SA** (210 km) — 25 min + lunch.
- Charge at **Ebina SA** (410 km) — 20 min.
- Arrive Tokyo by 4-5 PM.
- **Total charging cost:** ¥3,500-5,000.

**Option B: Drop EV and Fly/Shinkansen Back**
- Return your EV at Osaka Station or Kansai Airport.
- Take the Shinkansen back to Tokyo (2.5 hours, ¥14,500/adult, ¥7,250/child).

## Complete Cost Breakdown (Family of 4, 6 Days)

| Expense | Budget (¥) | Mid-Range (¥) |
|---------|-----------|---------------|
| EV rental (6 days, Nissan Leaf e+) | ¥48,000-60,000 | ¥72,000-90,000 |
| Charging (total trip, ~1,200 km) | ¥8,000-10,000 | ¥8,000-10,000 |
| Toll roads (Tokyo-Osaka-Tokyo) | ¥24,000-26,000 | ¥24,000-26,000 |
| Accommodation (5 nights) | ¥50,000-75,000 | ¥100,000-150,000 |
| Food (6 days, family of 4) | ¥60,000-90,000 | ¥120,000-180,000 |
| Activities/parks | ¥25,000-40,000 | ¥50,000-80,000 |
| **Total** | **¥215,000-301,000** | **¥374,000-536,000** |

**Vs Shinkansen + hotels:** Same itinerary but using Shinkansen (2 adults + 2 half-fare kids) costs ¥87,000-108,000 for transport alone. Add taxis at every stop and you save ¥40,000-80,000 with the EV.

## EV-Specific Tips for Japan

### Winter Range

Winter in Japan (December-February) can see 0-5°C in Tokyo, well below zero at Mt. Fuji viewpoints. Expect 25-35% range reduction. Plan an extra charging stop on winter trips. Pre-condition the battery before DC charging.

### e-Mobility Power Card (Must Have)

Available at any FamilyMart for ¥1,650. This card works at over 8,000 chargers nationwide, including most CHAdeMO stations at highway SAs. Register it in the Enel X Way app to view rates and history.

### Driving on the Left

Japan drives on the LEFT (like Hong Kong, Thailand, Malaysia, Indonesia, Australia, UK). If you're from a right-side country, take 30 minutes to familiarise yourself in a quiet area before hitting the highway.

### Parking Can Be Expensive

Central Tokyo and Osaka parking costs ¥300-600 per 30 minutes. Hotels often charge ¥1,000-2,000 per night. Factor this into your budget. The ETC parking discount (using your Highway ETC card) works at many city parking lots — ask your rental company.

### Language Barrier

English signage is limited at some highway SAs. But most charging stations have multilingual instructions (English, Chinese, Korean). The Enel X Way app is in English. Google Translate with camera mode is your best friend.

### What to Pack

- [ ] CCS2 to CHAdeMO adapter (if renting a Tesla)
- [ ] Type 2 AC cable (for hotel charging)
- [ ] e-Mobility Power card (get at FamilyMart)
- [ ] ETC card (should come with rental)
- [ ] International Driving Permit
- [ ] Sunshades (Japanese summer is brutal)
- [ ] Kids' tablets with downloaded shows
- [ ] Google Translate on phone (download Japanese language pack)
- [ ] Cash — many charging stations accept cards, but some older ones are cash-only

## Seasonal Guide

| Season | Months | EV Impact | Best For |
|--------|--------|-----------|----------|
| Spring | Mar-May | Excellent | Cherry blossoms, mild temps |
| Summer | Jun-Aug | Moderate | Festivals, but hot (30-35°C) |
| Autumn | Oct-Nov | Excellent | Autumn leaves, cool weather |
| Winter | Dec-Feb | Reduced range | Clear Fuji views, onsens |

**Cherry blossom season (late March-early April):** Book accommodation 2-3 months in advance. Charging stations will have queues — plan an extra 15-minute buffer.

**Obon week (mid-August):** Japan's busiest travel period. Highway congestion can add 2-3 hours. Avoid if possible.

## FAQ

### Can I drive Tokyo to Osaka without stopping to charge?

No. Even the longest-range EVs (Tesla Model S: 650 km WLTP) cannot comfortably do 510 km with elevation changes, AC usage, and highway efficiency. A charger stop is essential. Plan at least one 30-minute stop.

### Is there charging at Universal Studios Japan?

Yes — Universal Studios Japan's main parking lot has CHAdeMO 50kW + CCS 50kW chargers (6 slots). You can charge while you enjoy the park.

### Do I need an International Driving Permit for Japan?

Yes, absolutely. Japan requires an IDP issued under the 1949 Geneva Convention. It's valid for 1 year. Your home country driving license is NOT sufficient. Apply at your local automobile association before travelling.

### Are Japan's highway chargers reliable?

Generally yes, with some caveats. NEC and Nissan-branded CHAdeMO chargers at major SAs have 90%+ uptime. Smaller SAs and older chargers can be out of service. Check PlugShare before departing each leg. If a charger is down, the next SA is almost always within 30 km.

### What is the best EV for Japan's Golden Route?

The **Nissan Leaf e+** (62 kWh, 458 km WLTP) is the ideal choice for Japan — it uses CHAdeMO (Japan's most common fast charger), has plenty of space, and is available at most rental agencies. The **Tesla Model 3** is also excellent if you prefer Superchargers (there are 3 on this route).

### Are there overnight charging options in Kyoto's traditional machiya?

Most traditional machiya (townhouses) do NOT have EV charging — they're old buildings. Stay at a hotel with charging in central Kyoto and use public transport for temple visits. Kyoto Station's hotel complex (Hotel Granvia) has EV parking.

## The Bottom Line

Japan's Golden Route from Tokyo to Osaka is now a world-class EV road trip. The Tomei and Meishin expressways are well-stocked with CHAdeMO and CCS chargers at every major service area. With a Nissan Leaf e+ or similar EV, you can comfortably drive the 510 km route with just two 25-minute charging stops — which double as family breaks with food, clean toilets, and souvenirs.

The savings vs the Shinkansen for a family of four are substantial (¥40,000-60,000), and the experience — driving under Mt. Fuji, stopping at Nagoya for the Railway Park, feeding deer in Nara, and arriving in Osaka with a charged battery — is something no train ride can replicate.

faq.question: Can I drive Tokyo to Osaka without stopping to charge?
faq.answer: No. Even the longest-range EVs need at least one 30-minute charging stop for the 510 km route. Plan 2 stops on the Tomei Expressway for a stress-free trip.

faq.question: What charging connector does Japan use?
faq.answer: CHAdeMO is the standard DC fast-charge connector. CCS is becoming common at newer highway stations. Tesla Superchargers use Tesla plug (adapter available).

faq.question: Do I need an International Driving Permit?
faq.answer: Yes. Japan requires an IDP under the 1949 Geneva Convention. Without it, you cannot legally drive. Get it from your home country's automobile association before travel.

faq.question: Best EV for this trip?
faq.answer: Nissan Leaf e+ (62 kWh, 458 km WLTP) — uses CHAdeMO, available at all major rental agencies, good family space.
